kinds.d: Glassy coating made to be fired onto ceramics.

x.d: Green glaze coloured by a small amount of iron oxide in reduction firing, from China, named by seventeenth-century Europeans.
Deep black iron glaze that breaks to ginger brown at edges, imitating Chinese Jian ware of the southern Song dynasty; oil-spot crystals form in oxidation.
Japanese glaze from the sixteenth century with a satiny white to creamy surface and orange where it breaks, prized for tea wares.

kinds.d: Coloured slip-based decoration applied under or without glaze.
Liquid wax painted on ceramics to keep glaze off.
Kit for mending broken pottery with lacquer and gold powder in the Japanese manner.

x.d: Repair with urushi lacquer, including ki urushi, red bengara urushi, mugi urushi (lacquer and wheat flour) and sabi urushi (lacquer and clay), cured in a humid furo for 2 days to 2 weeks and dusted with gold, silver or platinum.
x.dt: lacquer type · metal powder · cure time

brands.d: Brush-on glaze maker whose Stroke & Coat line fires cone 06 to 10.

traditions.d: Japanese mending of broken pottery with urushi lacquer dusted with gold, silver or platinum.
traditions.tech: urushi lacquer joins and fills, cured in a humid furo, then metal powder is applied
traditions.mat: urushi, wheat flour, clay, gold, silver or platinum powder
traditions.auth: lacquer seams cured over days and dusted with metal powder rather than epoxy glue
